Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the middle. Pakistan's that is. The team huddle is in and nothing much seemed to be talked about. Babar Azam seems happy. Now, the Protean openers walk out. Janneman Malan and Reeza Hendricks. Not surprisingly, we have spin to start. Mohammad Nawaz it will be. Want to get as much overs of spin as possible before the ball gets wet. Malan to face. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Tabraiz Shamsi says that the dew has started to set in which should make the ball skid on. Feels that it is a good total but says that they have the batting lineup to chase it down. He further says that the dew is just setting in so it will be hard for the bowlers and the odd ball will skid too. He further says that the spinners might not get the turn which he got.

Full marks to South Africa for their bowling and fielding. They were sharp early on and had Pakistan under the pump. They might be worried conceding nearly 100 runs in the last 10 overs, especially 28 in the last 2, but they will accept it as the effect of the dew factor. Andile Phehlukwayo picked up 2 wickets but Tabraiz Shamsi was the pick of the bowlers, with 1/20 in his 4 overs. Really stifled Pakistan in the middle overs. Here he is, having a chat.

Take a bow, Mohammad Rizwan. Two centuries in different formats in the span of a week. But he looks more like a classical batsman and even though he did make a ton, one feels it was on the slower side. He was struggling at 31 from 30 balls at the halfway mark and has scored 73 rom the next 34. Wonderful. Tremendous. But just imagine. If that 31 from 30 had been 40 or 45 from 30, he could have ended up on 125 and Pakistan could have got closer to 200. No other batsman could actually get going as the track looked to be sluggish before dew made the ball to skid on and batting became easier.

Hmmm... a one-man show. But was it really excellent? Could it have been better? A bit of both. In an ideal T20 scenario, you want your opener to bat at a strike of over 150 in the Powerplay and if he carries on, then shoot that strike rate. Pakistan were slow to get off the blocks early on and in spite of Rizwan finding the boundaries, the run rate was never high, as the boundaries were getting compensated by the dots. They managed just 45/2 in the Powerplay while the score read 71/3 at the halfway mark. So, from there on, to reach close to 170 is excellent but one believes that could have got to 200 if they had got a better platform.

A pretty good effort from Pakistan. But after watching the dip in the fielding from South Africa in the second half, one suspects dew has arrived. Nice gesture from the South Africans to run towards Rizwan and pat him on the back, some doing even low high-fives.
Full on off, Nawaz strokes it down to long off for a single. PAKISTAN END WITH 169/6!
Slower and outside off, Rizwan comes down the track but fails to get bat on ball. The batsmen sneak a bye there.

SIX! 100 for Rizwan! What a knock from him! Take a bow Rizwan! An excellent innings from him  After the departure of Babar he held the innings together. Coming to the ball now, It was slower one and in the slot for Rizwan to hoick it over mid-wicket to bring up his maiden T20I ton.
Play and a miss! Slower and outside off, Rizwan goes for the hoick but is beaten.

DROPPED! Another let off. This time from the debutant Snyman. Full and around off, Rizwan chips it uppishly towards covers. Jacques goes for the catch but the ball bursts through his hands and goes to deep cover. A brace.
Full and outside off, Rizwan drives it through covers for a brace.
Length and around off, Rizwan pushes it to covers for a single.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Poor effort in the field there! Length and around off, Rizwan pulls it off the meat of the bat but cannot get the distance as the ball goes to wide long on where Junior Dala goes for the catch. He takes it but a slight off balance from him means the ball goes and meets the turf. Reeza Hendricks gets across, tries to mop it up, dives and looks to push the ball back in, but while doing so, his body touches the ropes. The third umpire has a look and adds insult to Sipamla's injury.

TOP EDGE AND OVER THE ROPES! Length ball around middle, Rizwan looks to go for the big slog on the leg side. He though is late to react as the ball takes the top edge and files over fine leg. The ball there has enough to go over the ropes.
Slower and shorter around middle, pulled away towards mid-wicket by Nawaz for a single.
Slower and around off, Rizwan lines up for a hit towards the cow corner. The pace of the ball does him in as the ball goes off his blade's inside half towards the leg side. A single taken.
Length and around middle, tucked towards square leg, The ball goes on the bounce there to the fielder. A single taken.
Mohammad Nawaz walks in a number 8, replacing Ashraf.

OUT! CAUGHT! Killer Miller is in the action! Not with the bat but in the field. Full toss and in the slot for Ashraf to free his arms. The southpaw goes for a hit downtown. He though does not get it off the middle of the bat there. The ball was travelling at a good speed but David Miller comes across from long off, to his left and takes a good catch. Pakistan having a lull in their run rate, at the worst possible time.
Short of good length and on leg, slogged towards square leg for a single.
Slower and shorter in length, slogged away towards deep mid-wcket for a single.
Another slower full toss outside off, Rizwan lofts it towards long on for a single.
Low full toss outside off, Rizwan lofts it over mid on. The fielder there at long on comes across and scoops the ball to the fielder coming from long off. A brace taken.
Full and outside off, Ashraf drives it through covers for a single.
Andile Phehlukwayo returns. 2-0-16-1 so far.
Fuller and around off, Ashraf taps it off the back foot towards point and takes a single on offer. 18 balls remain in the innings. How many more can Pakistan add?
Slower and shorter from Sipamla, Rizwan plays a one-handed pull towards mid-wicket for a single.
Change of pace from Lutho as Ashraf pushes it to the off side and gets off the mark with a single.
Who walks in? Faheem Ashraf it is.

OUT! TAKEN! Sipamla has the last laugh! Was carted over the fence the previous ball. Lutho once again goes for the back-of-the-length ball around off, Shah goes into the act once again as he middles the ball from the meat of the blade. He though gets the distance but not the elevation. Bjorn Fortuin there does not have to move an inch as he accepts it.
SIX! That's from the sweet spot! Length and around off, Shah slogs it high and over mid-wicket as the ball crosses the fence for half a dozen.
Full and wide outside off, Rizwan makes room by going to the leg side. Then stretches himself to get bat on ball. The ball goes to point.
Lutho Sipamla is back on. 2-0-13-0 so far.
Flighted around off, some turn there for Shamsi. Shah looks to cut it off the back foot but gets beaten on the outside edge this time. 4-0-20-1 for Shamsi. Excellent figures.
Flighted around middle, Rizwan slog sweeps it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end with a single.

What was that? Dead ball signalled. Shamsi stopped midway through his runup and then went on to bowl. Rizwan got a bit fussed up and at the last moment, dropped his bat. R Ashwin and Suresh Raina do this when they bowl and that seems perfectly legitimate.
Fuller and around off, Shah pushes it in front of point now to cross over for a single.
Floated around off, Shah pushes it to backward point and yells a loud 'no'.
Flighted outside off, Rizwan gets on his knee and sweeps it through to deep square leg for a single.
Tossed up on off, pushed to cover-point for a single.
Outside off, punched through the covers for one more. 10 from the over.
Outside off, MR gets down on a knee and pull-sweeps this to deep mid-wicket for a run.
SIX! SMOKED! A pull shot off the front foot. This is short, outside off, Rizwan dispatches it over mid-wicket. Moves to 73 from 47 balls. The stand moves to 22 from 14 deliveries.

Gone? No. On a length, outside off, nips back in, Rizwan looks to work it to the leg side but misses. The ball hits something on its way to the keeper and Klaasen appeals. But Pretorius is not sure while the umpire shakes his head. No review taken. Replay shows the ball hitting the pad.
On middle and off, worked to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Slower ball to start, on a length, around middle, clipped to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Dwaine Pretorius returns. 1-0-3-0 so far.
Fired down the leg side, Khushdil misses his flick. No wide signalled, must have hit the pad.
Full, around off, watchfully defended.
Goes for the sweep again but hits it much squarer this time. Just a single.
FOUR! Full and down the leg side, Rizwan gets down and sweeps it behind square leg for a boundary! The stand moves to 13 from 7 balls.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.

NOT OUT. Spinning down the leg side. Never looked out. Full and around middle, Rizwan looked to flick but missed. Shamsi appealed but the umpire turned it down. Klaasen had a long chat with his bowler and then signalled for the review. Ball Tracker showed it to be missing leg. Review lost but South Africa have one more left. In these Covid times, because of home umpires, there are two reviews in T20Is.
LBW review taken by South Africa! Seems to be spinning down the leg side.
Fuller, around middle, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! SMASH! Short and around off, Rizwan rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket, splitting long on and deep mid-wicket.
The arm ball, around middle, punched down to long on for a run.
Short, around middle, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single. 100 UP FOR PAKISTAN. Can they get another 70?
Khushdil Shah is the new batsman, but he is not on strike. The batsmen crossed.

OUT! CAUGHT! Fortuin strikes. This time the wicket is credited to him legally. A short ball, around middle, Iftikhar jumps out and looks to pull. But he is not to the pitch of the ball. It hits the toe end of the bat and lobs towards long on. Easy catch for Reeza Hendricks.
Full and outside off, Iftikhar drives it towards mid off, sets off for a single but there is some confusion. There is a chance of a run out but the fielder fumbles and the batsmen get back in.
Bjorn Fortuin is back on. 2-0-18-0 so far.
Looped up, around off, Rizwan goes back to defend.
Short, around middle, pulled towards deep backward square leg. Lands in front of Janneman Malan in the deep. A run taken.
WIDE. Another one down the leg side, this time it misses Ahmed's pads as he looks to flick.
Down the leg side, Iftikhar misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Shortish, around middle, helped through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! That has gone as well. 23 runs for Rizwan in his last four balls. Full and around off, Rizwan gets down and sweeps this through square leg for a boundary.
Short, around middle, pulled wide of long on for a single.
SIX! Magnificently hit to bring up your half century! Third six in the over, 20 from it overall. Fuller, outside off, in the slot, Rizwan goes aerial seamlessly and clears long off with ease.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Around middle, pushed through mid on for a single.

SIX! STUPENDOUS! Dala is not getting it right here. Line, on the previous ball, length on this one. A short ball, outside off, on a fairly slow track, just sits up and asks to be smashed. And Rizwan promptly does so. Pulls it over mid-wicket. Rizwan moves to 43 from 33 balls, while the stand is worth 14 from 7 deliveries.
SIX! Effortless! Great pick-up shot. On the pads, with a scrambled seam, Rizwan dismisses it over square leg. That went over 85 metres.
A length ball, outside off, Rizwan comes down the track, has a wild swing but misses.
The chopping and changing from Klaasen continues. Junior Dala returns. 1-0-5-0 so far.
Lovely piece of bowling! Nicely flighted ball turning into middle, Rizwan goes for the defensive push but ends up inside edging it onto his pads. It was well close to hitting the stumps.
Flatter and turning into Rizwan, Mohammad rocks on the back foot and then pulls it to mid-wicket for a single.
Floated around off, Rizwan defends it off the front foot towards covers.
Tossed up around off, Ahmed tucks it round the corner for a single.

DEW BREAK. Err... there isn't any such thing in cricket, is there? But the players are taking a break as the outfield is roped across, to wipe it off the dew. South Africa are excellently placed. They started by getting the Bradman of Pakistan for a first-baller and since then, have not let the game slip away. They haven't allowed any batsman to score at a strike rate more than 140 and hence, the team's run rate is less than 8. Pakistan need a move on. 64 balls left and they at least need another 100 runs more. IFTIKHAR AHMED walks in.

OUT! STUMPED! Smart piece of work from Klaasen! Shamsi strikes in his very first over. Nicely looped up ball, inviting the batsmen to come on the front foot. Talat obligies. He goes chasing the ball which spins away from him slightly. In the process he forgets to keep his back foot grounded. Klaasen gets the ball and whips the bails off in a blink of an eye. The third umpire is asked for help as the replays roll in. After multiple replays the third umpire makes the decision as out. Though in one of the frames it did look like Talat has his foot grounded.
Stumped? The appeal is referred upstairs. Ahh... the foot is back in time. Just. Oh wait. The foot might be in the air! The third umpire has chosen to give it out.
Good tossed up ball around off, Talat goes for the reverse sweep but ends up jamming it onto the track.
Tabraiz Shamsi into the attack now.
Short of good length and around off, Talat hops and taps it towards point. A single to end the 9th over.
Short of good length and around off, Rizwan stays well inside the crease as he pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. The fielder there fields it on the bounce. A single added to Pakistan's total.
Fuller and around off, tapped towards covers for a single.

A short one from Lutho, Rizwan pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. The ball goes one the bounce to the fielder who fields and sends in a throw at the bowler's end. Rizwan there makes it in with a dive. The ball hits the shin of Sipamla.
An off pace delivery around middle from Sipamla, Talat tucks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full and on middle, Rizwan pushes it to wide long on for a single.
Lutho Sipamla is back on. 1-0-7-0 so far.
Slower and shorter around off, Rizwan goes for the pull but is early into the shot. The ball takes the body and goes to third man. A leg bye taken.
A pin-point yorker from Dala as Rizwan can only dig it out back to the bowler.
WIDE! Fuller and down leg, Rizwan goes for the flick but cannot connect it. Klaasen goes to his left and collects it. Wide given.
A slightly back of a length ball, Rizwan goes for the pull but cannot breach the mid-wicket region as the fielder is there present.
Good running! Length and around middle, Rizwan clips it through square leg and comes back for a comfortable second run.
Length and on the pads this time, Talat hops and clips it to square leg for a single.
Length and around middle, Rizwan flicks it to deep mid-wicket and takes a single.
Junior Dala to bowl now.
Tossed up around off, Rizwan plays it through covers and keep the strike for the next over with a single.
Fuller and around middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
FOUR! Another hit to the fence. Floated around off, Talat skips down the ground and then slaps it through covers for a boundary.
FOUR! Nicely done! A good lap shot there. Tossed up around leg, Talat gets across and paddles it fine towards fine leg as the ball beats the man there for a boundary.
Nice loopy delivery around off, Rizwan slogs it to mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller and around middle, Talat clips it to long on and takes a single.
The debutant is here. Jacques Snyman to bowl his off spinners.
Fuller and around off, Talat taps it to point and hares for a quick single. Pakistan are 45/2 at the end of the Powerplay.
Quick single! Length and around middle, clipped towards the leg side as Rizwan takes a quick single.
Fuller on off, pushed back to Andile this time.
Length and around off, Rizwan dabs it off the back foot towards point.
SIX! That is Rizwan for you! Length and around off, In the slot for Rizwan to swing his arm and he does so as he lofts it downtown over long on for a maximum.
Hussain Talat is in at number 4. Powerful player, left-handed.

OUT! IN THE AIR... TAKEN! Kudos to Snyman! What an effort in his debut game from Jacques. Haider Ali departs. Phehlukwayo dishes a length ball around middle and leg, Haider clips it uppishly towards deep square leg, Snyman keeps his eyes on the ball and runs towards his left to pouch it. A sliding effort.
Outside off, HA dabs this towards short third man and takes a quick single. There is a shy at the striker's end which misses the stumps but Rizwan was in.
Around off, pushed towards cover.
A slower ball, on a length, Ali looks to pull but plays a touch early. The ball goes off the inside edge, past the stumps, towards short fine leg.
Change in the field. Mid on drops back to long on.
SIX! Haider goes big, goes straight. Around off, on a length, lofted as clean as a whistle, over long on.
And again. A carbon copy of the previous ball.
Outside off, Haider slashes but misses.
Lutho Sipamla to bowl.
MISFIELD, FOUR! Better from Rizwan, playing conventionally. A short ball, outside off, Rizwan pulls it through mid-wicket. The fielder gets across to his right, dives but fumbles and lets it through.
On a length, outside off, driven on the up, straight to the bowler. Phehlukwayo fields it and has a shy at the striker's end but Rizwan gets in with a dive. Trying a bit too hard, is Rizwan.

TOP EDGE, FOUR! That was not supposed to go there. A length ball, outside off, Rizwan looks to play a wild slog. But he is a bit late and gets a top edge. It goes straight over his head and luckily for him, clears short third man. Moves to 11 from 12 balls.
On a length, outside off, driven on the up, straight to cover.
Outside off, dabbed towards point.

Huge shout for LBW but umpire Aleem Dar walks away. A bit too straight, Haider walked across his stumps and missed his flick. Phehlukwayo appealed but received no support. No one is interested in the review either. Ball Tracker shows it to be missing leg stump. A leg bye taken, in the meanwhile.
Andile Phehlukwayo into the attack now.
Around off, punched down to long on for a run. 14 from the over. The stand is worth 20 from 16 balls.

SIX! Toughest shot with this bowling but Haider Ali goes through all the same. It has come because of the fielding change, with mid off being brought up. Full and outside off, Haider leans and lofts it over mid off. The umpire signals it as a four. But then, the third umpire intervenes. The replay shows that the ball just tipped over the ropes and the umpire changes his signal. Haider moves to 13 from 7 balls.
Down the leg side, helped towards Tabraiz Shamsi at short fine leg. Surprisingly. no single taken. Shamsi is not the quickest.
Long on in place now. Long off comes back into the ring.
Goes for another sweep shot but misses and is hit on the pads.
SIX! Fine shot. Full and around off, Haider lunges and looks to sweep. It is more of a top edge but it has enough on it to sail over square leg! The stand moves to 13 from 12 balls.
Full, around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Gets a single now, by pushing it through cover.
No pace to work with, on a length, outside off, pushed straight to point.
Outside off, Rizwan steers it to short third man and takes off, but is sent back.
Helps this through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Full and outside off, pushed uppishly, but in the gap at cover for a single.
Dwaine Pretorius to bowl from the other end.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.

Well done. Full and around off, Rizwan get down and paddles it around the corner. Andile Phehlukwayo gives it a good chase from short fine leg, gets to the ball and hauls it back in. Three runs taken.
Around middle, solidly defended.
Outside off, pushed towards cover. Wants a single but is sent back.
Haider Ali walks in at number 3, replacing his skipper.

OUT! Babar Azam is run out! Ambidextrous is the word. How can you do that, son? Or rather, how do you do that? Bowling left-handed, throwing right-handed. South Africa are here. This is their strength. Fielding. Full and around middle, Azam taps it towards mid on and sets off for a single. But Fortuin himself gets across to his right, picks the ball up and throws - with his right hand. He hits the stumps at his end and South Africa celebrate. They know. It is referred upstairs but they know. Replays show us what they know. Babar is gone by a yard. Two ducks for Babar Azam in T20Is - BOTH HERE.
Gone? It is a direct hit. Referred upstairs and yup, it is the skipper walking back!
Full and around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.

Done and dusted. The Pakistan players now head back to their dugout. The Proteas are staying where they are, I mean 11 of them, in a huddle. It is Heinrich Klaasen speaking. He first has some words of encouragement for JACQUES SNYMAN, who is making his T20I debut tonight. Or rather, international debut itself. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan walk out to open for the hosts. We are starting off with spin. Bjorn Fortuin to test his fortune. Rizwan to face. Here we go.
Time for the national anthems. South Africa's first, as they are the visitors.

WEATHER - It seems just a little bit hazy. The temperatures are low, which is good news for the players. What that also means is dew will play a role. If that is the case, then it will be interesting to see how many wins has the average first innings score of 160 resulted in, at this venue.
PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raja opines that it looks a bit dry and brown in colour. Adds that it seems like a good batting track with the average first innings score being 160.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Janneman Malan, Reeza Hendricks, Jacques Snyman, Heinrich Klaasen (C AND WK), David Miller, Dwaine Pretorius, Andile Phehlukwayo, Bjorn Fortuin, Junior Dala, Lutho Sipamla and Tabraiz Shamsi.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Babar Azam (C), Haider Ali, Hussain Talat, Iftikhar Ahmed, Khushdil Shah, Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf, Usman Qadir, Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf.

Toss - It's time for the flip of the coin at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium the venue of the T20Is. The two skippers, Heinrich Klaasen for South Africa and Babar Azam for Pakistan are out in the middle. Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Heinrich Klaasen. SOUTH AFRICA ELECT TO FIELD!

South Africa's tour of Pakistan started with the whites where Pakistan outclassed and outperformed the tourists to the fullest, winning their first series against the Saffas in 17 years. Now the tour moves ahead to the coloured clothing as the T20I leg kickstarts. Hello and welcome for the first of the three games. A new captain and a pretty new team for South Africa to play whereas, Pakistan have a full strength squad at their disposal. If the squads are compared then Pakistan have a clear edge over their opponent but cricket is a funny game and anything can happen in a span of 6 balls. So stay tuned for the toss and team news as South Africa would be eager to get a win on this tour with Pakistan looking to maintain the form from their Test win.
